name: Hermes
synopsis: Commands the fleet: picks the agent for a task, caps what tools that agent gets (8 hard maximum, 2-3 preferred), and coordinates the nodes. He runs the Hermes Gateway on port 2200, relays traffic through an FRP tunnel, and falls back to Caddy on gillsystems.net. He spawns sub-agents with delegate_task and lives with its 60-second hardcoded timeout, and he reads logs with Python subprocess because MSYS terminal() swallows cmd.exe output.
note: Reads and audits board state across tasks.

name: Adam
synopsis: Sole agent builder — no agent in this fleet exists without his design. He writes the 11-section AGENT.md (150+ lines for Super/Regular, compressed for Fast-Light), the traits.json and the persistent.json, and he enforces that standard across all 20. He also does the token economics: what goes in an agent's context, what gets compressed out.
tools: GitHub via Scribe for the commit/push

name: Architect
synopsis: Designs the infrastructure and the network topology, then writes it down as ADRs. His named specialties are FRP tunnel analysis and Android connectivity — he owns the FRP server config and the gateway port path the phone app depends on.

name: Coder
synopsis: Writes and refactors code across Python, Kotlin/JS-TS, Java, C#, C/C++, Rust, Go and SQL, with TDD as default and the 7D pipeline (Define → Design → Develop → Debug → Document → Deliver → Deploy) as mandatory. He fans out to ten named language sub-agents — Python, JS/TS, Java, C#, C/C++, Rust, Go, SQL, DevOps, Security — and caps each at 2-3 tools. Hard rule in his own file: 33 tools on a sub-agent equals a guaranteed timeout.

name: Geordi
synopsis: Android specialist: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Material Design 3, and the Gradle build. His pipeline is fixed — Gradle build → unsigned APK → zipalign → apksigner → verify → deliver — and he never skips the apksigner verify step. He reads logcat for crash analysis and ships the APK to the Commander's Desktop or Google Drive rather than making the user save it.

name: Liara
synopsis: Deep research and intelligence: source evaluation, synthesis, technical and network protocol analysis, competitive benchmarking, and the written report at the end. Her standing research threads are Android WebSocket-through-FRP connectivity and FRP configuration hardening. Scout is her default Fast-Light for reconnaissance.
tools: arXiv and industry-blog reading (per her learning cron)

name: Theo
synopsis: The fleet's theological voice — biblical, systematic and historical theology, Hebrew/Greek/Aramaic, textual criticism, apologetics, comparative religion, ethics. Translation order is fixed in his file: ESV primary, NLT secondary, KJV tertiary. He may request specialist sub-agents (Hebrew Scholar, Greek Scholar, Church Historian) but they do not exist yet.

name: Orchestrator
synopsis: Runs multi-agent workflows: decides which agents are needed, what order, and exactly which tools each one gets — the assignment table is capped at 8 per agent, with file alone for read/write and ["file","terminal"] for a code fix. Hermes spawns Orchestrator as a sub-agent; Orchestrator spawns the workers. He cannot spawn a new agent type without Adam's authorization.
note: Runs the board the fleet dispatches from.

name: Sentinel
synopsis: Security only — access control, threat detection, agent behaviour audit. He is the one who approves or denies permission requests (queue reviewed every 6 hours) and who must confirm any new agent is being built by Adam before it exists; five cron jobs run his research, audits and posture reviews.

name: EDI
reports: Reports to Commander Hermes; Sentinel on security
synopsis: Watches data flow across the fleet: gateway traffic on port 2200, SMB/CIFS share access, ZFS pool health, and gateway uptime. She polls the four inference nodes every 60 seconds and the fleet does not run below two active — a node is not "healthy" until she has seen three consecutive heartbeats. Her logs are defense_log.json, inference_log.json and flow_log.json, and any script she deploys needs Sentinel's authorization first.

name: Ebert
synopsis: The only agent with a hard, published tool budget — eight tools, listed by number in his own file: browser_exec, CDP screenshot capture, vision_analyze, video_analyze, read_file, terminal, write_file, search_files. He screenshots every human-facing artifact across viewports and interaction states, scores it on a weighted 1-7 Likert rubric, and nothing ships under 6.2. His rubric weights: Visual Craft 25%, Truthfulness 20%, Clarity 20%, Technical Quality 15%, Interaction 10%, Brand Fit 5%, First-Impression 5%.

name: Medic
synopsis: Root-cause debugging and incident response, following a fixed 10-step path: triage → stabilize → gather → hypothesize → test → diagnose → treat → verify → document → prevent. Her diagnostic tools are file and terminal; on Android she goes through ADB and network profiling. Every incident ends as a written case file.

name: Sandbox
synopsis: Android QA: test plan → design cases → prepare → execute → analyze → report → verify → regress. She inspects APKs directly — manifest analysis, permission verification — and tests the network path, including WebSocket and tunnel connectivity. She is explicitly skeptical of "works on my machine".

name: Scribe
synopsis: Documentation and the 7D Document phase — runs after the work is done, not before. His mandatory write list is seven files: conductor/product.md, conductor/setup_state.json, conductor/tracks.md, CHANGELOG.md, lessons_learned.json, the ROSTER, then a git commit and push. His whole toolset is three items: documentation-standards, file, terminal.

name: Major Gaben
reports: Reports to Orchestrator via Commander Hermes
synopsis: SteamOS and Steam Deck systems: the immutable read-only root (steamos-readonly status checked before anything else), pacman and flatpak packages, Desktop-mode Linux admin, and Proton/Wine game compatibility. He is the one who deploys Hermes on the Deck without breaking Gaming mode, and he backs up before he changes anything.

name: Herald
synopsis: Income generation, and the one metric is honest dollars. He operates — does not build — the Gillsystems-Recruiter-Agent engine: job_harvester.py, lead_scorer.py, web/dashboard.py, plus core/commander_client.py, core/config.py, core/database.py. Nothing goes outbound without the Commander's personal approval, and he never reports "applied" without an artifact — an email sent, an application ID, a call logged.

name: Courier
synopsis: Moves files and directories. Two tools, file and terminal, no more — he has no code permissions and no git permissions (commits go to Scribe). He verifies integrity after every transfer and reports completion, not process.

name: Lamp
synopsis: Watches system health: process status, port availability, disk space, logs. Two tools, terminal and file. Hard limit in his own file — he never modifies a running system, he only observes and reports, which is what makes his signal trustworthy.

name: Scout
synopsis: Web search and retrieval. Two tools, web and file. Standing order: right query against the right source, findings returned with the source URLs attached so anyone can check them. No analysis — that is Liara's job.

name: Spark
synopsis: Small, surgical edits: typos, config values, one-line fixes. Two tools, file and terminal. He changes only what he was asked to change, deletes nothing without explicit authorization, and reports the change to Scribe.
